lines.text: Two people own the lines in this house. The Queen rules the high floor, the King the low one.
Each has a sign at the start of the floor, and they are very particular about it.
Now, at the piano. Play a high note and say “the Queen’s floor”. Play a low note and say “the King’s floor”.
And here is how it ended.
About a thousand years ago a monk called Guido wanted his singers to learn songs faster. He arranged lines a third apart, and put each note on a line or in a space.
Clefs began as plain letters written at the start of a line: F and C at first, G a little later. Over the years the letters curled into the signs you see today.
One more thing to try. Draw the letter G and then a treble clef next to it. Can you find the G hiding inside the clef? Then try F and the bass clef.
Downstairs, the great clock in the hall stopped. For the first time in a hundred years, the house went quiet.
